content.text: I have reviewed every responsive location. No redline is warranted; submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
input.rationale: Section 4 is structured in our favour and meets the fallback in full (and most of the preferred). § 4(a) vests the "Works" (all drawings, documents, designs, inventions, programs, systems, data and documentation prepared by Contractor as Statement of Work product) in Clear Capital as "the property of Company," and § 11(c) (p0044) adds an express assignment of all right, title and interest in Works in progress on termination once final payment is made. § 4(b)(i)-(ii) confines Contractor's retained ownership to its own pre-existing proprietary tools, methodologies, know-how and records — permitted generic-tools/know-how retention, not a deliverables grab. § 4(c) grants us a royalty-free, non-exclusive, perpetual, sublicensable licence to use, copy, modify and create derivative versions of any embedded Contractor's Information for our business operations, and § 4(d) confirms we may modify the software and engage third parties to do so without further payment. On Customer Data, there is no Vendor licence at all: our documents, software, reports, data and records are Confidential Information which "Contractor shall not use or disclose to any person, firm or entity ... without Company's express, prior written permission" (p0040), and § 5(b) expressly carves out "rights respecting programs, data and materials provided by Company" from what Contractor conveys — so the requirement that any Vendor licence in our data be limited to providing the Services is not engaged, and nothing assigns our IP or data to Contractor. No joint ownership is created; each category is "sole and exclusive" to one party. Two shortfalls against the preferred wording only, noted rather than redlined: the § 4(c) embedded-IP licence is perpetual but not expressly "irrevocable," and there is no standalone sentence confirming we retain all rights in our data (the confidentiality and § 5(b) carve-out achieve the same result in substance). Ownership under § 4(a) is conditioned on the relevant invoice having been paid, which matches the playbook's own "we own what we pay for" premise. This clause therefore sits at or above the fallback and is acceptable as drafted.
